question: Two countries are blazing a trail in the fight against illegal immigration: - Firstly, Italy, thinking outside the box, has entered into a migration agreement with Albania to transfer migrants rescued at sea to Albanian detention centres. These Italian-run centres will process asylum applications. - Secondly, the post-Brexit United Kingdom has signed a deal with Rwanda to send rejected asylum seekers there.

These two kinds of agreement complement each other: they either allow for asylum applications to be processed in third countries or for asylum seekers to be deported to other third countries. In light of the above: 1.

Is the Commission exploring all avenues to increase the number of bilateral agreements with third countries on processing asylum applications in or deporting rejected asylum seekers to those countries?
Will Tunisia and Mauritania receive the agreed payments for helping us combat illegal immigration?
Finally, could the Commission elaborate on any new deals, such as the one recently concluded with Egypt, and also on the talks with Morocco?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2024) 1- The Pact on Migration and Asylum1 reflects a whole-of-government and whole-of-route approach to migration management, ensuring coherence and effectiveness among actions taken by the EU and Member States. The Commission works in a Team Europe approach to deepen comprehensive partnerships based on mutual interests.

EU legal framework does not provide for extraterritorial processing of asylum applications. EU’s external action aims at supporting third countries hosting refugees and constantly increase bilateral agreements with third countries on readmission of their nationals who do not have the right to stay in the EU.

2- The Commission is implementing the Memorandum of Understanding with Tunisia2 and the EU-Mauritania Joint Declaration on a Migration Partnership3 to deepen strategic and comprehensive partnerships of mutual interest, including migration security, economic development, energy and trade.

This includes funding to fight against migrant smuggling, promote security and stability, humanitarian aid for refugees and support to host communities. 3- The Union and Egypt Strategic and Comprehensive Partnership4 aims deepening their shared stability, peace and prosperity. It covers six key pillars and is underpinned by a financial and investment support of EUR 7.4 billion.

The EU has a long-standing cooperation with Morocco5. In 2022, the Commission launched an anti-smuggling operational partnership and, in 2023, new cooperation programmes with Morocco on green transition, migration and reforms.

EU financial support on migration covers notably integrated border management, fight against smuggling and trafficking in human beings, protection, support to labour migration and assisted voluntary returns.
